archetype.name: Fringe Contender (guard-led, glass-crashing)
archetype.definition: A team coming off a lottery season whose hot start and strong underlying ratings put it in the playoff conversation, while a shaky frontcourt and a three-game sample keep it short of a sure thing.

report.headline: Jerome and the offensive glass make 3-0 real, though not this real
report.take:
Memphis arrives at 3-0 after a 25-57 season that ranked 26th on the site, and this start is built on margin more than luck. The Grizzlies have outscored opponents by 34 points, carry a Net Rtg of 11.4 (6th) and pair a 119.7 ORtg (5th) with a 108.3 DRtg (9th). The W vs Pt Diff of 1 says one of those wins, the 111-108 escape at Golden State, was a coin flip. The margin implies two wins, not three. The 82-win pace is what three games of perfection projects and nothing more.

Two things are driving it. The first is Ty Jerome. He has 104 points on a 68.9 TS % while using 34 percent of possessions, with an 11.5 BPM that ranks him first of 92 on the shooting-guard tab. That is why the backcourt grades an A, and Jaylen Wells (74 TS %) has given him efficient help. The second is effort stats that usually travel. A league-best 37.8 ORB %, ten points above the league average, has Memphis 2nd in REB %. On defense, opponents take only 23.3 percent of their shots at the rim (4th), against 32.1 last season. Those are structural changes, not hot shooting.

The numbers hide a frontcourt that is producing volume without efficiency. Cameron Boozer leads the team in minutes and has 35 rebounds, but his TS % is 43.2 and Jerami Grant's is 44.7. Grant, Quinten Post and GG Jackson II all carry deeply negative On-Off figures. Zach Edey has been the frontcourt's best piece, with 19 rebounds in 44 minutes and a +50.1 On-Off, and he is listed day-to-day. The offense also leans on a 38.1 3P %, four points above the league. It gives away possessions at a 15.2 TOV % (22nd) and rarely gets to the line. The shooting is the part most likely to cool.

The trajectory is a team clearly better than last year's, closer to the 2024-25 version (48-34) than the 2025-26 one. Expect regression from Jerome's efficiency and the three-point luck. The rebounding and rim deterrence should keep the Grizzlies on the right side of .500.

strengths.title: Ty Jerome runs an elite offense
strengths.body: Jerome is carrying a heavy usage load at elite efficiency, and the offense ranks 5th by ORtg around him. A 68.9 TS % at 34 USG % will not hold all season. Even a meaningful drop leaves him a top-tier creator, so the backcourt A grade has real substance behind it.

strengths.title: League's best offensive rebounding team
strengths.body: Memphis is grabbing 37.8 percent of its own misses, first in the league and ten points above average. That is worth second chances every night, and it covers for the turnover problem. Last season the figure was 24.7. Even if it settles well below 37.8, crashing the glass is an effort-and-size trait that tends to persist better than shooting.

strengths.title: Keeping opponents away from the rim
strengths.body: Opponents are taking just 23.3 percent of their shots at the rim (4th), down sharply from 32.1 last season. They are also shooting a below-average 62.7 there. That shape is behind a defense that ranks 9th after finishing 23rd a year ago. It looks like a scheme change rather than variance.

concerns.title: Frontcourt volume without efficiency
concerns.body: Boozer leads the team in minutes but is shooting a 43.2 TS % with a -5.2 BPM. Grant sits at 44.7 TS % with a -30.3 On-Off. The frontcourt grades C-, and most of its non-Edey minutes have been a drag. Boozer's rebounding is real. His shot quality is the swing variable for how good this team can be.

concerns.title: Edey's health matters more than minutes suggest
concerns.body: Edey has played only 44 minutes over two games. In them he has the best On-Off among the bigs and a pile of rebounds. He is day-to-day, and the alternatives at center (Post at -34.3 On-Off) have struggled. Prolonged absences would test whether the rim deterrence holds.

concerns.title: Sloppy and shooting-dependent offense
concerns.body: A 15.2 TOV % ranks 22nd, and the FT Rate of 28.1 ranks 21st. The offense is leaning on a 38.1 3P %, four points above league average, to cover both. When the threes cool, the turnovers and the lack of free throws will show. One of the three wins was already a three-point-range game.

trend.note: Three games, three wins, two by comfortable margins (123-103 over Utah, 123-112 at Sacramento) and one tight one at Golden State. The big movement is year over year, from a 25-57 team to a top-ten Net Rtg.

weekAhead.headline: Three soft defenses around one real test in Portland
weekAhead.body:
Four games, and three of them come against defenses ranked 28th (Utah), 27th (Sacramento) and 25th (New Orleans) by DRtg. Memphis has already beaten the Jazz and Kings by double digits. The final two games are at home. A 3-1 week is the baseline expectation, and a sweep is realistic.

The exception is Wednesday's game at Portland. The Blazers are 2-0, 2nd on the site, with the league's best Net Rtg at 24.5 and opponents shooting 45.1 eFG % against them. Their numbers come from just two games. Even so, they protect the ball (11.3 TOV %, 2nd), which removes one of Memphis's edges, and their wings grade A+ against a Memphis wing group rated D+.

keyMatchups.title: Jerome against Utah's leaky guards
keyMatchups.body: Utah allows 45 points a game to shooting guards, 28th in the league, and a 123 DRtg overall. That is exactly where Jerome lives. Expect another big scoring night to open the week.

keyMatchups.title: Portland's defense versus Memphis shooting
keyMatchups.body: The Blazers have held opponents to a 22.6 3P %, first in the league in a two-game sample. Memphis's 38.1 3P % will meet its stiffest test here. The glass may decide it, but Portland's 75.8 DRB % (5th) blunts that edge too.

keyMatchups.title: Home stand against soft interiors
keyMatchups.body: Sacramento rebounds only 68.4 percent of opponents' misses (25th), a gift to Memphis's offensive glass. New Orleans has allowed 30.67 points a game to centers, the most in the league. Both games set up for Boozer and Edey to get easy volume, and for Boozer to find some efficiency.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Edey is available, and whether Boozer's shooting improves against the soft interiors of Sacramento and New Orleans.

restOfSeason.body:
The rebounding and the rim-deterrence profile look like genuine changes from last season. They support a team that ranks comfortably in the top half of the league on both ends. What will regress is the shooting: the 38.1 3P % and Jerome's near-70 TS % are unlikely to hold. The turnover rate also leaves a thin margin once the threes stop falling. Netting it out, this looks like a solid winning team, more like the 48-34 version of two seasons ago than a contender.

I project 40 to 48 wins and a Net Rtg settling between roughly +1 and +5. The upside case needs Boozer to turn his volume into efficient scoring and Edey to stay on the floor. The downside case is a frontcourt that keeps bleeding points whenever Edey sits.

confidence.note: Three games; ratings and player lines are extremely noisy this early.
